subject: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0

messages.author: ee0aba41dd5807ef
messages.subject: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
Hi,

I just updated one of my computers to the newest version of R and unexpectedly came across this error:

Full Error:
Calculating the Gelman-Rubin statistic for 11 variables....
Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : 'tim' is not character or numeric
Error in blavaan(mod4, data = dat, jagcontrol = list(method = "rjparallel"),  : 
  blavaan ERROR: problem with jags estimation.  The jags model and data have been exported.


I tried it on another computer and had no problem. Only happened on a Windows machine with R 3.3.0 and
after just downloading the blavaan v0.1-4.34

Reproducible example:

mod.noGrowth <-"
i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4
i~0*1
i~~1*i
t1~~1*t1
t2~~1*t2
t3~~1*t3
t4~~1*t4
"

dat <- lavaan::simulateData(mod.noGrowth,sample.nobs=300,model.type="lavaan")

mod4 <- ' i =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4
      s =~ 0*t1 + l1*t2 + l2*t3 + 1*t4'

fit4 = bgrowth(mod4, data=dat, 
               jagcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"))

messages.author: ee0aba41dd5807ef
messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
Reverting to R 3.2.2 took care of the problem. So maybe just something that could pop up in 3.3.0.

Ross

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
I also noticed this when I upgraded an ubuntu computer to 3.3.0. I fixed it by re-installing lavaan, runjags, and/or blavaan from CRAN (can't remember which of these solved the problem) before moving to the blavaan devel version.

I'm not sure why this happened, and I didn't see anything obvious in the 3.3.0 NEWS.

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
I looked at this some more, and it seems like there is a bug in the runjags package caused by a modification to how R 3.3.0 handles time objects. I suspect you will only see it when convergence="auto" and when the model does not converge quickly. But I also contacted the runjags maintainer.

Ed

messages.author: e7839a344d6e5c5b
messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
On Thursday, May 12, 2016 at 2:48:35 PM UTC-4, Ed Merkle wrote:
I looked at this some more, and it seems like there is a bug in the runjags package caused by a modification to how R 3.3.0 handles time objects. I suspect you will only see it when convergence="auto" and when the model does not converge quickly. But I also contacted the runjags maintainer.

I ran into this on Ubuntu as well, but with R 3.3.1 2016-06-21. As you say, it pops up only when tries out 'converge="auto"' and for me after at least half an hour of runtime. I tried 3 times but it crashed with the 'tim' error each time. lavExport: https://www.dropbox.com/s/3gur5qqw13p9n1b/2016-07-28-blavaan-timerror.tar.xz

I did an update.packages() and upgraded everything I could, which included runjags, and updated to version 2.0.4-2 (2016-07-25). It successfully ran then, giving me runtime messages like

    blavaan NOTE: Posterior predictives with missing data are currently very slow.
    Consider setting test="none".
   
    Loading required namespace: rjags
    module lecuyer loaded
   
    Auto-run JAGS
   
    Running a pilot chain...
    Compiling rjags model...
    Starting 7 rjags simulations using a Fork cluster with 7 nodes on host ‘localhost’
    Simulation complete
    Finished running the simulation
   
    Calculating the Gelman-Rubin statistic for 47 variables....
    The Gelman-Rubin statistic was above 1.05 for 30 parameters after 9000 iterations taking 53.4 minutes (multi-variate psrf = 27.796).  This may indicate poor convergence.
    Maximum time limit exceeded; chains unconverged.  Try restarting the simulation using the end state values of the chains provided.
    Calculating autocorrelation and summary statistics...
    Returning UNCONVERGED simulation results

So upgrading runjags seems to've fixed it.

--
gwern

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
On Thursday, July 28, 2016 at 6:25:56 PM UTC-5, gwern branwen wrote:

So upgrading runjags seems to've fixed it.

Thanks for the report, it is good to see that the new version of runjags is now on CRAN. I will soon set "auto" to be the default convergence option.

I have also not forgotten the benchmarking but am currently in the midst of restructuring some internal functions (to support complex equality constraints, among other things).

Ed

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Error possibly a result of R 3.3.0
parts:
I recently set "auto" to be the default convergence option. I am not entirely happy with auto convergence because it takes a really long time (and, at least for exploratory modeling, we can often get by with fewer iterations). So I might switch the default back to "manual". Regardless, the functionality is there.

Ed
